To capture the authentic, chaotic atmosphere of a sprawling mid-century Italian-American wedding, director Francis Ford Coppola essentially threw a real two-day party on a Staten Island location and instructed his extras to freely improvise, eat, and drink. Amidst the highly structured interior scenes happening concurrently in the Don’s study, one of the most iconic moments was famously unscripted: Coppola found a stray cat wandering the Paramount lot and spontaneously dropped it into Marlon Brando’s lap just before cameras rolled. The feline purred so loudly over Brando’s muffled delivery during his opening scene that most of the actor’s dialogue had to be completely re-recorded in post-production, permanently cementing a happy accident into cinematic history.

The Godfather (1972), directed by Francis Ford Coppola, starring Marlon Brando, Al Pacino, James Caan, Diane Keaton. As the aging patriarch of an organized crime dynasty transfers control of his clandestine empire to his reluctant youngest son, a violent mob war threatens to tear their powerful family apart.
